problem: Reinforcement learning post-training of generative models is computationally prohibitive, limiting the practical adoption of RL-based alignment methods.
approach: TreeGRPO recasts the denoising process as a search tree where multiple candidate trajectories branch from shared noise samples, enabling efficient prefix reuse and multi-child branching for multiple policy updates per forward pass.
contribution: TreeGRPO achieves 2.4× faster training while establishing superior Pareto frontier in the efficiency-reward trade-off space compared to GRPO baselines.

problem: Maintaining consistent low-rank approximations of sequentially arriving data while minimizing solution changes is a challenging online optimization problem.
approach: The paper develops algorithms that provide sequences of rank-k subspaces approximating optimal low-rank decompositions with bounded recourse, showing upper and lower bounds for both additive and multiplicative approximation guarantees.
contribution: The paper proves recourse bounds ranging from O(k/ε log(nd)) for additive approximation to improved bounds of k^(3/2)/ε² poly log(nd) for multiplicative approximation on integer matrices.

problem: Vision-language models produce biased image captions with uneven descriptive granularity across image elements and hallucinated descriptions of non-existent objects.
approach: ScaleCap proposes debiasing via heuristic question answering that progressively injects visual details and contrastive sentence rating that identifies and eliminates hallucinations through offline contrastive decoding.
contribution: ScaleCap-annotated 450K images used for LVLM pretraining leads to consistent performance gains across 11 benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating robotic manipulation policies typically requires large-scale simulation sampling with high time costs and provides only a single scalar score without interpretability or user-customization.
approach: ManipEvalAgent conducts adaptive, multi-round evaluations using code generation to construct tasks and VLM-based video understanding to provide user-instruction-centric, fine-grained policy analysis without massive sampling.
contribution: ManipEvalAgent significantly reduces evaluation time compared to traditional simulation benchmarks while reaching comparable conclusions.

problem: Pre-trained models adapted for continual learning suffer from catastrophic forgetting and potential misalignment between task-specific classifiers and the adapted backbone across multiple tasks.
approach: Local Classifier Alignment (LCA) introduces a novel loss to better align classifiers with backbone as it adapts, following a model-merging approach for consolidating task knowledge into a unified backbone.
contribution: LCA often achieves leading performance on standard continual learning benchmarks, sometimes surpassing state-of-the-art methods with a large margin.

problem: Existing counterfactual explanations modify more features than necessary, reducing clarity and actionability by not minimizing the necessary edits.
approach: COLA refines counterfactuals by computing optimal transport couplings between factual and counterfactual sets and using Shapley-based attribution to select minimal feature edits while preserving target effects.
contribution: COLA achieves the same target effects with only 26-45% of the original feature edits across four datasets, twelve models, and five CE generators.

problem: Existing 3D-LLM evaluation benchmarks do not reliably measure genuine 3D spatial reasoning, as text-only models exploit textual shortcuts rather than demonstrating 3D understanding.
approach: Real-3DQA provides rigorous evaluation that filters out easy-to-guess questions and introduces a structured taxonomy for assessing 3D reasoning; 3D-reweighted training uses negative samples via explicit 3D-relation alignment.
contribution: Real-3DQA confirms existing 3D-LLMs struggle with spatial relationships when simple cues are removed, and 3D-reweighted training substantially enhances performance.

problem: Visual Prompt Tuning variants suffer from unstable training dynamics with gradient oscillations, shallow-layer prompt stagnation, and cross-layer mismatches that degrade convergence and performance.
approach: Prompt-Agnostic Evolution (PAE) models prompt dynamics from frequency-domain shortcuts and imposes global Koopman-based linear transformations across layers with Lyapunov-inspired error-amplification constraints.
contribution: PAE accelerates convergence by 1.41× on average and yields 1-3% gains on 25 datasets across multiple downstream tasks.

problem: Early Bongard Problem datasets used synthetic images or high-level features that don't fully capture the complexity of recognizing fine-grained abstract visual concepts from limited examples.
approach: Bongard-RWR+ generates 5400 instances by using a VLM pipeline: Pixtral-12B describes curated images, Flux.1-dev synthesizes new images, and humans verify faithful concept representation.
contribution: VLMs consistently struggle with discerning fine-grained concepts, highlighting limitations in abstract visual reasoning across diverse BP formulations.

problem: Vision-language models exhibit unstable performance under variations in natural language prompts, posing challenges for reliable real-world deployment.
approach: Promise uses meta-learning with dual-loop finetuning where the inner loop adapts token embeddings across varied prompts and outer loop optimizes for unseen prompt variants, plus adaptive prompt weighting and token-specific learning rates.
contribution: Promise consistently reduces prompt sensitivity and improves performance stability across 15 benchmarks spanning base-to-novel generalization, cross-dataset transfer, and domain shift.

problem: Static, manually curated benchmarks for Computer-Use Agents are narrow, contamination-prone, and diverge from real-world, user-driven evaluation needs.
approach: Computer Agent Arena provides an open-source platform with cloud-hosted dynamic environments, anonymous execution, and human-preference-driven evaluation converting preferences into structured feedback on 2,201 votes across 12 agents.
contribution: Computer Agent Arena reveals striking ranking reversals relative to static benchmarks and identifies capability gaps like long-horizon memory and fine-grained action failures.

problem: Black-box privacy auditing of differentially private learning algorithms relies on fixed canary sets that may not be optimized for detecting privacy violations.
approach: The paper develops a method using metagradient descent to optimize the auditor's canary set, improving the effectiveness of membership inference attacks.
contribution: Optimized canaries improve empirical lower bounds for differentially private image classification models by over 2× in certain instances, with transferability to larger models trained with DP-SGD.

problem: Vision-language foundation models like CLIP create strong global alignments but are limited in generating precise region-specific representations for localized image understanding.
approach: MaskInversion optimizes an embedding token by comparing its explainability map to a query mask, keeping the foundation model frozen and using gradient decomposition to simplify computation.
contribution: MaskInversion generates context-aware embeddings for localized captioning, image generation, and open-vocabulary retrieval, demonstrating capabilities on PascalVOC, MSCOCO, RefCOCO, and OpenImagesV7.

problem: Concept erasure in diffusion models faces a robustness-retention trade-off: hardening against adversarial attacks often degrades model utility, while retention-focused methods lack robustness.
approach: AEGIS replaces handpicked targets with an Adversarial Erasure Target optimized to approximate the semantic center of erased concepts, using Gradient Regularization Projection to preserve utility without auxiliary data.
contribution: AEGIS simultaneously improves robustness against adversarial prompt attacks and retains model utility, hardening diffusion models against state-of-the-art attacks.

problem: Approximate machine unlearning introduces privacy risks: adversaries with access to original and unlearned models can exploit their differences for membership inference or data reconstruction.
approach: WARP uses neural network symmetries via weight teleportation to reduce gradient energy of forgotten samples and increase parameter dispersion while maintaining accuracy on retained data.
contribution: WARP reduces adversarial advantage by up to 64% in black-box and 92% in white-box settings across six unlearning algorithms while maintaining retained-data accuracy.

problem: Molecular editing struggles to balance precise property optimization with structural preservation due to limitations of string-based or continuous representations in capturing discrete graph structure.
approach: MolEditRL uses a discrete graph diffusion model pretrained on source-to-target reconstruction, followed by editing-aware RL fine-tuning that optimizes editing decisions under explicit graph constraints.
contribution: MolEditRL achieves 74% improvement in editing success rate while using 98% fewer parameters compared to state-of-the-art methods, with comprehensive evaluation on MolEdit-Instruct (3 million examples).

problem: Kronecker compressed sensing requires efficient sparse recovery algorithms that leverage the hierarchical structure of Kronecker product measurement matrices.
approach: The paper develops a hierarchical multi-stage sparse recovery framework tailored to different sparsity models (standard, hierarchical, Kronecker-supported) with theoretical guarantees via restricted isometry property analysis.
contribution: The multi-stage algorithm achieves comparable recovery performance to state-of-the-art techniques while substantially reducing run time through hierarchical processing.

problem: Image super-resolution generative models rely on self-attention's quadratic complexity, creating computational bottlenecks that limit practical deployment of photorealistic SR systems.
approach: LinearSR resolves training instability in linear attention via Early-Stopping Guided Fine-tuning, mitigates perception-distortion trade-offs with SNR-based Mixture of Experts, and establishes lightweight guidance via precision-over-volume TAG.
contribution: LinearSR achieves state-of-the-art perceptual quality with exceptional efficiency, with core diffusion forward pass in 1-NFE and competitive multi-step inference time.

problem: Existing agentic coding benchmarks cover limited task scope and lack automated evaluation approaches for end-to-end feature development spanning multiple commits and pull requests.
approach: FeatureBench provides execution-based evaluation via test-driven task derivation that traces unit tests along dependency graphs to identify feature-level coding tasks, with automated scalable collection from open-source repositories.
contribution: FeatureBench curates 200 challenging tasks and 3825 executable environments from 24 repositories; state-of-the-art Claude 4.5 Opus achieves 11.0% success rate compared to 74.4% on SWE-bench.

problem: Diffusion models are vulnerable to memorization where they reproduce training data rather than generating novel outputs, but theoretical understanding of memorization mechanisms remains limited.
approach: The paper develops a dual-separation result through statistical estimation (showing ground-truth score function doesn't minimize empirical loss) and network approximation (empirical score requires scaling network with data).
contribution: The theoretical insights guide a pruning-based method that reduces memorization while maintaining generation quality in diffusion transformers.

problem: Discrete diffusion models rely on factorized reverse processes that struggle to learn target distributions in few steps, necessitating long, computationally expensive sampling procedures.
approach: The paper introduces learnable noising (forward) process for discrete diffusion using non-Markovian formulation with learnable marginal and posterior distributions, trained end-to-end under the standard variational objective.
contribution: Learnable forward process enables few-step generation while maintaining factorized generative process and matching the target distribution.

problem: LLM performance in program synthesis and mathematical reasoning is fundamentally limited by pre-training corpus quality for code and mathematics.
approach: The paper introduces SwallowCode and SwallowMath datasets via systematic rewriting: SwallowCode uses four-stage pipeline (syntax validation, pylint filtering, LLM rewriting) on The-Stack-v2; SwallowMath removes boilerplate and reforms into step-by-step explanations.
contribution: Within 50B token budget, continual pretraining yields +17.0 on HumanEval and +12.4 on GSM8K over baseline models.

problem: Novel view synthesis typically assumes ideal, clear inputs and struggles under real-world image degradations like blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow.
approach: ReSplat jointly estimates restored images and gaussians for clear scene representation, using 3D gaussians from diffusion sampling as self-guidance for multi-view consistent image restoration.
contribution: ReSplat significantly outperforms existing methods across blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow conditions, delivering superior visual quality for robust NVS.

problem: Evaluating LLM reasoning ability is complicated by extensive parametric world knowledge, where benchmark performance often reflects factual recall rather than genuine reasoning capability.
approach: SynthWorlds constructs parallel corpora with identical structure but in real-mapped and synthetic-mapped worlds, enabling clean separation of reasoning complexity from factual knowledge via mirrored tasks.
contribution: SynthWorlds reveals a persistent knowledge advantage gap, demonstrating that knowledge acquisition mechanisms reduce but do not eliminate this gap.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models discard spatial-reasoning-critical visual tokens during pruning because existing methods focus only on semantic relevance.
approach: IVC-Prune reveals that LVLMs establish implicit visual coordinate systems via Rotary Position Embeddings and identifies IVC tokens by analyzing RoPE properties; it retains IVC and foreground tokens via two-stage semantic discovery.
contribution: IVC-Prune reduces visual tokens by ~50% while maintaining ≥99% performance and achieving improvements on several benchmarks.

problem: Computing Pareto sets for expensive multi-objective optimization problems requires efficient, scalable methods that balance multiple conflicting objectives.
approach: SPREAD uses Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models to learn conditional diffusion over decision space and refines candidates via adaptive multiple gradient descent with Gaussian RBF-based repulsion for diversity.
contribution: SPREAD matches or exceeds leading baselines in efficiency, scalability, and Pareto front coverage across multi-objective optimization benchmarks.

problem: Radar-based precipitation nowcasting requires modeling high-dimensional spatiotemporal data under atmospheric uncertainty while maintaining computational efficiency for time-critical applications.
approach: FlowCast leverages Conditional Flow Matching for direct noise-to-data mapping in compressed latent space, replacing iterative sampling of diffusion models with rapid sample generation.
contribution: FlowCast establishes new state-of-the-art in probabilistic performance with significantly greater efficiency than diffusion objectives while maintaining high performance with fewer sampling steps.

problem: Federated inference methods lack robustness to attacks, leaving ensembles of distributed model predictions vulnerable even to simple adversarial perturbations.
approach: The paper formalizes robust federated inference using DeepSet aggregation with adversarial training and test-time robust aggregation to defend non-linear aggregators.
contribution: The composition of adversarial training and test-time robust aggregation surpasses existing robust aggregation methods by 4.7-22.2% in accuracy across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Small LLMs lack robustness in grade-school math reasoning and experience performance drops under distribution shifts like numerical changes or distracting clauses.
approach: AbstRaL promotes abstract reasoning through reinforcement learning on abstraction data, enabling LLMs to connect problems to symbolic tools; RL is shown to produce more faithful abstractions than supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: AbstRaL significantly mitigates performance degradation on GSM perturbation benchmarks and implicitly benefits OOD mathematical and general reasoning tasks.

problem: Estimating calibration error of binary classifiers from finite datasets requires practical, non-asymptotic methods without restrictive distributional assumptions.
approach: The paper provides upper bounds for classifiers with bounded-variation calibration functions and a method to modify any classifier so its calibration error is efficiently upper-bounded without impacting performance.
contribution: The paper provides non-asymptotic, distribution-free methods with practical procedures for measuring calibration error on real-world datasets.

problem: Agent evaluation is limited to coarse task success metrics that fail to reward intermediate behaviors, lack interpretability, and require expert design.
approach: AutoLibra transforms open-ended human feedback into concrete evaluation metrics by grounding feedback to behaviors, clustering similar behaviors, and using LLM-as-Judge evaluators with meta-metrics for alignment assessment.
contribution: AutoLibra induces more concrete agent evaluation metrics than previous benchmarks and enables agent improvement through self-regulation via induced metrics.

problem: Process Reward Models either treat reasoning steps in isolation or fail to align process rewards with final outcomes, causing ambiguous credit assignment and vulnerability to reward hacking.
approach: Conditional Reward Modeling (CRM) conditions step rewards on preceding steps and explicitly links to final outcomes, enforcing conditional probability rules to capture causal relationships among reasoning steps.
contribution: CRM consistently outperforms existing reward models across Best-of-N sampling, beam search, and RL, providing more reliable cross-sample comparison and robustness to reward hacking.

problem: Optimal transport-based flow matching (OT-FM) promises better training but requires expensive O(n²/ε²) operations per batch pair when using Sinkhorn algorithm, limiting practical adoption.
approach: The paper proposes semidiscrete optimal transport formulation that leverages finite-size target dataset by solving via SGD on dual potential vector of size N, matching freshly sampled noise at train time.
contribution: Semidiscrete formulation enables practical OT-FM scaling without batch-size limitations while maintaining theoretical promises.

problem: Multimodal Reward Models lack long-term reasoning capabilities and existing RL approaches for reward modeling often lead to training instability or collapse.
approach: R1-Reward reformulates reward modeling as rule-based RL task and proposes StableReinforce algorithm that refines training loss, advantage estimation, and reward design for stable training dynamics.
contribution: R1-Reward achieves 8.4% improvement on VL Reward-Bench and 14.3% on Multimodal Reward Bench, with further improvements as inference compute increases.

problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption code generation is error-prone due to semantic ambiguity, API misuse, and cryptographic insecurity risks, limiting practical adoption.
approach: FHE-Coder uses a three-phase agentic framework: Prompt Formalizer for secure parameterization, RAG module with scheme-specific knowledge, and automated Security Verifier for iterative validation and cryptographic correction.
contribution: FHE-Coder consistently generates code that is compilable, functionally correct, and verifiably secure across FHE schemes including TFHE and CKKS.

problem: Multimodal encoders for visual document retrieval scale dimensionality of representations, creating deployment obstacles while the modality gap limits pure vision-centric approaches.
approach: Guided Query Refinement (GQR) refines primary retriever's query embedding at test time using guidance from complementary text retriever's scores through lightweight dense fusion.
contribution: GQR allows ColPali-based models to match larger-representation performance while being up to 14× faster and requiring 54× less memory.

problem: RL-trained language model agents often struggle in tasks requiring active exploration and fail to efficiently adapt from trial-and-error feedback at test time.
approach: LaMer is a Meta-RL framework with cross-episode training for exploration and in-context policy adaptation via reflection, allowing agents to adapt without gradient updates.
contribution: LaMer improves performance by 11%, 14%, and 19% on Sokoban, MineSweeper, and Webshop respectively, with better generalization to more challenging unseen tasks.

problem: Existing Maps of Dynamics for robot operation use discrete spatial sampling and require costly offline construction, limiting applicability to dynamic human environments.
approach: NeMo-map proposes continuous spatio-temporal MoD representation using implicit neural functions that map coordinates to Semi-Wrapped Gaussian Mixture Model parameters, enabling smooth generalization.
contribution: NeMo-map achieves better accuracy of motion representation and smoother velocity distributions in sparse regions while remaining computationally efficient compared to baselines.

problem: Time-series forecasting increasingly demands causal predictions under interventional and counterfactual queries in multivariate systems beyond observational predictions.
approach: DoFlow uses flow-based generative models defined over causal DAGs, enabling coherent observational and interventional predictions through continuous normalizing flows.
contribution: DoFlow enables accurate system-wide observational forecasting, causal forecasting under interventional and counterfactual queries, and principled anomaly detection.

problem: Standard Sparse Autoencoders for feature extraction impose independence priors that fail to capture temporal dynamics and context-sensitive structure in language model activations.
approach: Temporal SAE decomposes representations into predictable and residual components via temporal inductive bias, capturing context-dependent and novel information separately.
contribution: Temporal SAE correctly parses garden path sentences, identifies event boundaries, and delineates abstract slow-moving from novel fast-moving information better than existing SAEs.
